finding: List-file-is-a-folder fix covers only the read path; add, remove and repoint still raise a raw OSError
why: add_repository, remove_repository and repoint_repository go through safe_write.update_locked, whose _read does target.read_bytes() (scripts/safe_write.py:78-79) and raises IsADirectoryError or PermissionError, not RepositoryListError, so setup gets the raw path error F4 reported.
fix: Wrap the update_locked calls (or give the transform path a pre-check on list_file().is_dir()) so an unreadable list raises RepositoryListError 'cannot be read' on every entry point.
evidence: Caller dispositions: 'a list file that is a folder is refused with "cannot be read"'; only _read_list (find_entry/all_entries) was changed; test_a_list_file_that_is_a_folder_is_a_list_error calls only rl.all_entries()

finding: Empty-path guard added to main_checkout only; find_entry('') and find_entry(path, root='') still read as the current folder
why: The F3 cause is normalize('') resolving to the cwd; find_entry calls normalize(path) and normalize(root) unguarded, so a blank lookup silently matches the current folder.
fix: Refuse a blank path in find_entry, or document that lookups accept a blank as the current folder.
evidence: find_entry: 'key = _key(normalize(path))' and 'base = normalize(root)'; main_checkout alone gained 'if not os.fspath(path).strip()'

finding: Deleting the retry back-off sleep in _read_list survives all tests
why: Both retry tests zero SWAP_RETRY_SECONDS, so no test observes that a refused read waits before retrying; without it the 11 attempts burn in microseconds and the swap race the fix targets is not covered.
fix: In the Windows retry test, monkeypatch rl.time.sleep to record calls and assert it is called with safe_write.SWAP_RETRY_SECONDS once per refused open.

finding: Generic-OSError branch of _read_list is unpinned on Windows (survived there)
why: The only test reaching `except OSError` is the list-file-is-a-folder test, which raises PermissionError on Windows, and busy_open only raises PermissionError; the branch is killed only where a directory open raises IsADirectoryError.
fix: Add a platform-independent test where busy_open raises a non-Permission OSError and assert RepositoryListError 'cannot be read' after exactly one open.
evidence: mutant: OSError branch raise -> `return []`; Windows run: 76 passed, 3 skipped (SURVIVED)
